newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Asia-Pacific nations pledge action, not words.
newsitem.headline: Asia-Pacific nations pledge action, not words.

text.p: Asia-Pacific leaders ended their annual summit on Monday and endorsed a detailed action plan for turning into reality APEC's goals of creating the world's biggest free trade region by 2020.

The plan is called the Manila Action Plan (MAPA) for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum and was finalised by trade and economic ministers who met for two days last week to prepare for the summit.
The ministers described these plans as so comprehensive they are "without parallel in other trade and investment liberalisation fora".
-- How APEC's 18 members plan to reduce tariffs gradually to zero by 2010 for developed members such as the United States and Japan and by 2020 for the less well off.
-- Reaffirms APEC's commitment to a voluntary, non-binding structure instead of the formal, legal structure of other trade groupings such as the European Union.
-- APEC's support for a leading role for the private sector in boost trade and investment in the region and in providing a "reality check" for political leaders and officials.
-- Plans for speeding up the movement of goods and people throughout the region by harmonising customs and immigration procedures.
-- APEC's commitment to improving its less developed members' ability to compete by fostering a programme of economic and technical cooperation.
-- Plans to demonstrate APEC's concern for small and medium scale enterprises by providing training resources and information on potential new markets.
